question: Violations of property rights of the Greek National Minority in Albania and their connection to the closing benchmarks of Chapter 23

According to a recent report, violent incidents occurred in Albania during residents’ reactions to tourist development, with members of the Greek National Minority among the injured, and the protesters raising the issue of protection of property rights12.
At the same time, similar protests by residents against beach fencing, restricted access, contested land use and lack of transparency in licensing have been recorded on the Albanian coastline.

3 Following the recent intergovernmental Conference of 26 May 2026 and the adoption of the Interim Benchmark Assessment Report (IBAR),4 Albania entered the final phase of accession negotiations, with Cluster 1 ‘Fundamentals’ including the rule of law, fundamental rights, functioning of democratic institutions and public administration.
The protection of property, access to justice and transparency in land expropriations or concessions are directly linked to the accession criteria. In view of the above: 1.
How does the Commission assess the allegations of infringement of property rights and lack of transparency in tourism development in Albania?
Does the Commission intend to include the property issue and the related allegations explicitly in Albania's accession dossier and evaluation reports?
Will the Commission ask the Albanian authorities to conduct an independent investigation into the incidents of violence and the licensing of the projects in dispute?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The Commission is closely monitoring developments in Albania as part of its EU accession process.

The quality and efficiency of the judiciary, and the respect and protection of fundamental rights, including the right to property and rights of persons belonging to minorities, are crucial components of the benchmarks under Cluster 1 – Fundamentals of the accession negotiations.

To assess Albania’s progress on its EU accession path, the Commission rigorously monitors all developments and continuously engages with the national authorities in all areas of the negotiations, including on the rights of persons belonging to minorities, property rights, freedom of association, access to justice and due process.

All ongoing projects in Albania must comply with the applicable legal framework and with the relevant accession negotiations benchmarks. Albania is expected to ensure effective judicial follow-up in any cases of alleged violence. The Commission will continue to engage with the national authorities to uphold the highest standards of rule of law and ensure the protection of fundamental rights.
